title: Separating Beads and Cells in Multi-channel Microfluidic Devices Using Dielectrophoresis and Laminar Flow
protocol: Design PCB electrodes to the desired geometry to generate a non-uniform electrical field.
Solder 16-gauge wire to the end of each printed metal electrode on the PCB.
Place the wire onto the end of the electrode.
Heat the wire with a hot soldering iron on the metal area of the PCB.
Feed a small amount of solder into the heated wire to fill the wire with solder.
Hold the wire in place while the solder cools after filling with solder.
Repeat the soldering process for each electrical connection on the PCB.
Mix base compound to curing agent at a 10:1 ratio for 5 minutes.
Pour liquid PDMS onto the prefabricated SU-8 master mold.
Remove air bubbles by exposing liquid PDMS to vacuum for a few minutes.
Repeat vacuum process if needed to completely remove all bubbles.
Cure the PDMS at 70 °C for 2 hours.
Remove the PDMS slab with microfluidic channels from the wafer using a razor blade carefully.
Punch holes in the PDMS slab for introducing fluids and cells into the microfluidic device.
Inspect the microfluidic device to ensure it is free of dust and debris.
Clean the PDMS using 3M Scotch Magic Tape.
Plasma bond the PDMS microfluidic channels to a clean no.0 thickness (80-130 μm) coverslip.
Heat the coverslip-microfluidic assembly at 100 °C for a minimum of 15 minutes.
Prepare low-conductivity media by mixing 8.5% sucrose + 0.3% glucose (w/v) in deionized (DI) water.
Place approximately 10 μL of mineral oil onto the PCB to ensure tight contact between the PCB and the coverslip.
Optionally coat the PCB surface with a very thin layer of black permanent marker or paint for decreasing electrode visualization.
Place the coverslip-microfluidic channel assembly onto the oiled PCB.
Press down gently to ensure good contact between the coverslip and oil.
Fill the microfluidic channels with DI water or low-conductivity media.
Introduce HT-29 cells into the channel reservoir.
Connect the output of a function generator to an AC power amplifier input.
Connect the amplifier output to electrode wires.
Cover all electrical wires and surfaces with electrical tape.
Set the function generator to produce a sine wave output of 1.0-1.5 MHz.
Adjust the amplitude of the output for the RF power amplifier to produce an output of 80-100V to the PCB.
Ensure the RF power amplifier receives an input voltage around 220-330 mV.
Verify laminar flow rates comply with DEP force requirements to move cells and beads within the main channel into target channels.
Consult with the PCB manufacturer to determine maximum operating voltages to prevent overheating or melting of the PCB.
Check equipment manufacturers' specifications for safe operating settings of function generators and power amplifiers.
Initiate DEP to sort cells and beads.
Cells experience positive-DEP in a non-uniform electric field within specified frequencies.
Polystyrene beads experience negative-DEP in a non-uniform electric field within specified frequencies.
Angle the metal electrode on the side of the single inlet channel.
Introduce DEP to guide beads to the side of the channel as they approach the trifurcation point.
Use DEP forces to pull beads into one of the side channels where laminar flow propels them down the channel.
Configure microfluidic channel structure and PCB electrodes as shown in Figure 2E-F.
Introduce a suspension of HT-29 cells and beads in low-conductivity media into the single inlet channel.
Apply DEP to retain HT-29 cells in the two left output channels.
Retain beads in the individual right output channel.
Observe characteristic 'pearl-chaining' behavior of collected HT-29 cells.
